A class is assigned only where the company claimed a size-dependent
relief, which is an assertion of being at most that size. Publishing more

revenue_ceiling.description:
Highest revenue this company can have had in this fiscal year without losing the size class it filed under — a hard upper bound, not an estimate.

Usually null, and that is the normal case rather than missing data: § 267 asks whether a company exceeds **at least two of three** criteria, so a size class alone permits any revenue. The bound only exists where a second criterion (balance-sheet total or employees) is already over its limit, which forces revenue under its own. Where it is null, no revenue bound follows from the class and none should be inferred.

size_basis.description:
Why `size_class` was assigned, as a stable code:

- `no_guv` — no profit-and-loss statement published (§ 326 Abs. 1)
- `rohergebnis` — P&L collapsed to a Rohergebnis (§ 276)
- `declared` — the filing states its own class
- `ceiling_balance_sheet` / `ceiling_employees` — a second § 267 criterion is over its limit, which tightened the class

size_class.description:
Statutory size class for this fiscal year — `kleinst`, `klein`, `mittelgross` or `gross` (§ 267 / § 267a HGB).

Derived from the reliefs the filing claims, so it is an exact statement about the company's own filing, not an estimate. **Null never means large.** It means the filing asserts no size — typically because a full profit-and-loss statement was published, in which case `revenue` carries the answer directly.

mode.description:
Delivery behaviour. **Default: `recurring`.**

- `recurring` — the **first** delivery is a snapshot of the current state. After that, you only get a notification when there is an actual update.
- `one_time` — keep polling at the configured `cadence` *until* the first successful delivery, then stop. Useful when:

SubscriptionType.description:
Slice of company data a subscription tracks. Two flavours:

- **Parsed-data** types — `details`, `history`, `shareholders`, `ubo`. The webhook body's `data` block carries a publish-date timestamp and `links` to the v1 endpoints that serve the parsed JSON.
- **Document** types — every `doc_*` value. The webhook body's `data.download.url` is a 7-day presigned URL to the PDF, so the customer can fetch the file directly without a follow-up API call. After expiry, `GET /v1/companies/{eu_id}/documents/download` mints a fresh URL.

**Coverage is not uniform across types.** German company law lets the smallest GmbH / UG (haftungsbeschränkt) replace the Articles of Association (Gesellschaftsvertrag / Satzung / Statut — the name varies by legal form) and the Liste der Gesellschafter with a single **Musterprotokoll** (model protocol) at founding. firmendata handles this asymmetrically by intent:

- `shareholders` **auto-falls-back** to the Musterprotokoll when no Liste der Gesellschafter is filed — pick this for cap-table tracking regardless of legal form.
- `doc_articles_of_association` does **not** fall back — pick `doc_model_protocol` when you need the founding deed of a simplified-procedure company.
- `doc_shareholder_list` does **not** fall back — pick `doc_model_protocol` for Musterprotokoll-only companies, or `shareholders` for parsed cap-table data that works for any GmbH/UG.
- `doc_*` subscriptions only fire for companies that actually filed the matching document; mismatches return `scrape_failed_file_not_found` until the document appears (use `mode=one_time` if you're waiting for a one-off filing).

| Value | What it tracks |
|---|---|
| `details` | Current company snapshot — identity, registered address, current board, share capital, and lifecycle status. The webhook body's `data.links.company_detail` resolves to `GET /v1/companies/{eu_id}` for the full parsed JSON. Available for every Handelsregister-registered company. |
| `history` | Chronological register history — every recorded change to company name (firma), seat (Sitz), capital, board, business purpose, etc. The webhook body's `data.links.company_history` resolves to `GET /v1/companies/{eu_id}/history` for the full parsed timeline. Available for every Handelsregister-registered company. |
| `shareholders` | Cap table — primarily from the **Liste der Gesellschafter** (list of shareholders), filed by GmbH and UG (haftungsbeschränkt). **Auto-fallback to Musterprotokoll:** companies founded via the simplified procedure under §2 Abs. 1a GmbHG do not file a separate Liste — their **Musterprotokoll** (model protocol) names the founders and their share allocations directly. firmendata handles this transparently: when no Liste has been filed, the `shareholders` subscription derives the cap table from the Musterprotokoll instead. So `shareholders` is the right subscription for cap-table updates regardless of which document the company filed. The webhook body links to `GET /v1/companies/{eu_id}/shareholders` for the parsed cap table. |
| `ubo` | Beneficial owners (**wirtschaftlich Berechtigte**) — natural persons who ultimately own or control the company, derived by walking the Gesellschafter graph. Each dispatch refreshes the cap-table document for **every** German GmbH/UG in the ownership chain (root and parents), not just the root, and fires when **any** chain member's Liste der Gesellschafter (or Musterprotokoll fallback) gets a newer publish date. The webhook body carries the full UBO report (graph, `beneficial_owners`, `potential_beneficial_owners`, `coverage` with `reason`) plus a per-node `chain` breakdown (`eu_id`, `depth`, refresh `status`, latest `publish_date`).  `coverage.status="partial"` means one or more unresolved branches carry effective share above 25 % at the root and could hide a UBO — `potential_beneficial_owners` lists those entities (foreign holdings, unlisted parents, depth-capped branches) with their summed effective share so KYC consumers can decide whether to escalate. `coverage.status="available"` with `has_unresolved_branches=true` means unresolved branches exist but are immaterial (combined share below the threshold or isolated by sub-threshold control links).  Transient per-node failures (e.g. `documents_temporarily_unavailable`, `platform_unavailable`) defer the dispatch — `latest_succeeded_publish_date` is not advanced and the next cadence retries; chain members that succeeded today are dedup'd at the registry layer so retries only re-hit the failed nodes' documents. Deterministic per-node outcomes (e.g. `file_unavailable`, `skipped_not_applicable` for non-GmbH chain members) are surfaced in the chain breakdown but do **not** block delivery — the rest of the chain still ships. |
| `doc_articles_of_association` | **Articles of association** document — Germany's constitutional company document, called **Gesellschaftsvertrag** (GmbH, KG, OHG, GbR), **Satzung** (AG, KGaA, eG, Verein), or **Statut** (some specific forms) depending on legal form. All three are filed under the same registry slot.  Webhook body's `data.download.url` is a 7-day presigned URL to the PDF — the customer can fetch the file directly without a follow-up API call. After the URL expires, `GET /v1/companies/{eu_id}/documents/download?file_type=articles_of_association` mints a fresh one.  **Not all companies have one.** Companies founded via the simplified procedure under §2 Abs. 1a GmbHG file a **Musterprotokoll** in its place — subscribe to `doc_model_protocol` for those. |
| `doc_company_registration` | **Initial company registration filing (Anmeldung zur Eintragung)** — the notarial document submitted to register the company. Webhook body carries a 7-day presigned download URL (`data.download.url`). Available for any newly-registered company; fires when a new Anmeldung is filed. |
| `doc_model_protocol` | **Model protocol document (Musterprotokoll)** — the simplified notarial founding deed for small GmbH and UG (haftungsbeschränkt) companies under §2 Abs. 1a GmbHG. Legally substitutes for **both** the Articles of Association and the Liste der Gesellschafter for these companies. The Musterprotokoll itself names the founders, their share allocations, and the basic company terms in a single document.  Webhook body carries a 7-day presigned download URL (`data.download.url`). Only companies founded via the simplified procedure have one; for everyone else this subscription reports `scrape_failed_file_not_found`. For **cap-table changes** — regardless of which document was filed — subscribe to `shareholders` instead (it auto-falls-back to the Musterprotokoll when no Liste has been filed). |
| `doc_shareholder_list` | **Liste der Gesellschafter** document — the standalone shareholder-list filing. Webhook body carries a 7-day presigned download URL (`data.download.url`).  Distinct from the parsed `shareholders` subscription: this tracks the **document itself** with no Musterprotokoll fallback, so a Musterprotokoll-only GmbH (founded under §2 Abs. 1a GmbHG) reports `scrape_failed_file_not_found` until they file a real Liste. For parsed cap-table updates that work for any GmbH/UG, subscribe to `shareholders` instead. |

info.description:
Programmatic access to German company data: register profile, filed
financial statements, company events, and current cap tables.

## Authentication

Bearer token in the `Authorization` header. Create and manage your
tokens in [API Key Settings](https://firmendata.com/de/account/api-keys).

## Data freshness

Every company endpoint exposes a `freshness` object so you can see, at
a glance, how stale the response is and which fetch mode produced it:

```jsonc
"freshness": {
  "object": "freshness",
  "last_checked_at": "2026-04-30T12:14:08Z",
  "realtime_fetching_status": "realtime_fetching_disabled"
}
```

`last_checked_at` is the UTC timestamp of the last successful refresh
of the underlying data slice from the German registries. Compare it
against your own staleness tolerance to decide which of the three
fetch modes below fits the call. `null` means the slice has never been
successfully fetched for this company.

There are three ways to consume the data, each with a different
freshness guarantee:

1. **Cached read (default).** Returns the most recent data we already
   have on file for the company. Cheapest and fastest. The data may
   be stale — the `freshness.last_checked_at` field tells you exactly
   how stale.

2. **Realtime fetch (`fetch_realtime=true`).** Refreshes the
   underlying slice from the German registries inline before
   responding. Costs more credits and adds upstream latency
   (typically several seconds, sometimes longer). On upstream
   failure, the response falls back to the most recent cached data
   for the company; `freshness.realtime_fetching_status` reports the
   outcome (`success`, `platform_unavailable`,
   `documents_temporarily_unavailable`, `file_unavailable`,
   `company_unavailable`, or `realtime_fetching_disabled`). When we
   have no record of the company at all, the endpoint returns 404
   the same as without `fetch_realtime`.

   On `/companies/autocomplete` and `/companies/search` the flag means
   *discovery* rather than refresh: the keyword is searched against the
   live German registers and companies not yet indexed by firmendata
   are added, appearing in the same response. For newly discovered
   companies the register documents and financial publications are then
   fetched in the background at no extra cost, so their full profile is
   available shortly after.

3. **Subscriptions.** The only mode that *guarantees* you eventually
   see fresh data: the dispatcher retries failed scrapes on the
   configured cadence and pushes a webhook (or queues an event) when
   something changes. Manage subscriptions via `/subscriptions`.

## Pagination

`/companies/search` uses opaque cursor pagination. Pass the
`pagination.next_cursor` value from a response back as the `cursor`
query parameter to fetch the next page. Cursors are not stable across
deploys.

## Rate limits

Every bearer token is capped at:

- **5 requests per second** (burst protection)
- **100 requests per minute** (sustained)

Both windows are enforced via a sliding-window counter, so limits degrade
gracefully across window boundaries. Every response — success or error —
includes headers so clients can self-pace:

- `RateLimit-Limit` — numeric limit of the tighter window currently applying
- `RateLimit-Remaining` — calls left in that window (never negative)
- `RateLimit-Reset` — seconds until the window resets
- `RateLimit-Warning` — present only when fewer than 10% of the window
  remains; a hint to slow down before hitting 429

When a limit is exceeded the server returns `429 Too Many Requests` with
a `Retry-After` header (seconds) and an RFC 7807 body. Rejected requests
do not consume the limit or any credits — they are free to retry once
the reset period elapses.

## Errors

All non-2xx responses follow [RFC 7807 `application/problem+json`](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7807).
The body always carries `type`, `title`, `status`, and `request_id` fields;
422 responses also include a structured `errors[]` array describing each
failed field.

## Stability

Object types carry an `object` discriminator (e.g. `"object": "company"`).
Nullable fields are always present (never omitted) and list fields default
to `[]` so client codegen output is stable across releases.

## Subscriptions

Stay current without polling on a fixed schedule: subscribe a single
company to one data slice and firmendata detects changes for you on the
cadence you choose, under `/subscriptions`. Pick one of three delivery
modes via `notification_type`:

* **Webhook** (`notification_type: "webhook"`) — firmendata POSTs a
  signed JSON body to your `webhook_url` on each change. Every request is
  HMAC-SHA256 signed; verify `X-Firmendata-Signature` against the
  `webhook_secret` returned at creation. Requires `webhook_url`.

* **Email** (`notification_type: "email"`) — a bilingual notification to
  `recipient_email` (with the register document attached as a PDF for
  `doc_*` subscriptions). Requires `recipient_email`.

* **Poll-only / async** (`notification_type: null` — the **default**) —
  no outbound delivery is performed. The dispatcher records each detected
  change as a `subscription_event`, and you retrieve the rendered payload
  by polling `GET /subscriptions/{id}/events` with the subscription
  (job) id returned on create. Omit both `webhook_url` and
  `recipient_email`. Ideal when you can't expose an inbound webhook
  endpoint and would rather pull changes on your own schedule.

`mode` selects `recurring` (deliver on every change) or `one_time`
(poll until the first successful delivery, then stop); `cadence` controls
how often the change check runs.

## Pricing

Every successful 2xx call deducts credits from your account; 4xx and 5xx
responses are free — no credits are spent on failed requests. Per-endpoint
credit costs, subscription pricing, plan allowances, and rate-limit tiers
are listed on the [pricing page](https://firmendata.com/en/plans) — the
single source of truth, so this spec links there instead of duplicating
numbers that can drift.

parameters.description:
Statutory size class under § 267 HGB. Multi-valued.

- `klein` — kleine Kapitalgesellschaft (§ 267 Abs. 1)
- `mittelgross` — mittelgroße Kapitalgesellschaft (§ 267 Abs. 2)

Read from the form of the filing itself: a company that omits its profit-and-loss statement (§ 326 Abs. 1) or collapses it into a Rohergebnis (§ 276) is claiming a relief only a company of that size may claim. Publishing *more* than required is permitted at every size and asserts nothing, so companies that file a full P&L carry no class — for those the reported `revenue` is the answer. The values are therefore not exhaustive, and selecting both is a real filter meaning "the filing form implies a size class", not a no-op the way selecting every `legal_status` is. `gross` is not offered because no relief can assert largeness: the company that claims nothing is exactly the large one.

Because the § 267 test is "does not exceed at least two of three" (balance-sheet total, revenue, employees), a class on its own does not bound revenue — it does so only where a second criterion is already over its limit. This filter is a size filter, not a revenue filter.

get.description:
Walk the company's ownership chain and identify the natural persons
who ultimately benefit from it.

For every German GmbH/UG encountered in the chain, the latest filed
Gesellschafterliste is read; recursion stops at natural persons,
foreign organisations, or any organisation without a German
Gesellschafterliste obligation. Each branch carries its direct share
percentage. Beneficial-owner attribution follows the German
"all-or-nothing" rule: each link in the chain is independently checked
against the 25 % control threshold (covering both >50 % majority
control and >25 % Sperrminorität under the BVA's post-TraFinG
reading of §3 Abs. 2 Nr. 3 GwG). The share attributed to a UBO is
the share at the final hop into the root — the actual capital stake
the UBO ultimately controls, not the multiplicative product.

- **Graph** — every node and directed `source → target` edge
  traversed during the walk. Use it to render an ownership tree or to
  audit which branches stop short.
- **Beneficial owners** — natural persons attributed more than 25 %
  of the root via direct holdings, controlled chains, or the sum of
  both, sorted descending. Empty when no person crosses the threshold
  (e.g. ownership diluted across many parties or the chain ends in
  unresolved organisations). Fictional UBO under §3 Abs. 2 S. 5 GwG
  is not surfaced.
- **Potential beneficial owners** — unresolved organisations whose
  summed effective share at the root crosses 25 % under the same
  all-or-nothing rule. The natural person(s) controlling each entity
  are candidate UBOs that we couldn't trace ourselves. Same-entity
  dedup across multiple chain positions is by `(name, registered_
  seat, country_code)`, so an org appearing twice with 15 % + 15 %
  surfaces as one entry at 30 %.
- **Coverage** — `coverage.status` distinguishes four states:
  `available` (chain fully resolved, OR remaining unresolved
  branches sum to ≤25 % effective share and cannot hide a UBO);
  `partial` (an unresolved branch could hide a beneficial owner —
  read `potential_beneficial_owners` and `coverage.reason`);
  `not_filed` (no cap table on file); `not_applicable` (legal form
  has no Gesellschafterliste obligation).
- **Completeness** — `has_unresolved_branches` flags any non-root
  unresolved node in the graph; whether that compromises the answer
  is encoded in `coverage.status` (`partial` if so, otherwise
  `available` with `coverage.reason` explaining why the unresolved
  branches are immaterial).
- **`fetch_realtime`** — optional. When `true`, refetch the latest
  Liste der Gesellschafter for every German GmbH/UG in the chain
  before building the graph. Adds noticeable latency (several seconds
  per company in the chain). Failures are surfaced via
  `freshness.realtime_fetching_status`; the graph still falls back to the most
  recent indexed cap tables when a refresh fails.

**Edge cases worth knowing:**

- **Control passes through 100 %, not the chain product.** A holds
  60 % of H, H holds 30 % of root → A is a UBO with
  `effective_share_percent = 30`, not `18`. Each link is checked
  independently against the 25 % threshold.
- **Sperrminorität counts as control.** A 26 % blocking minority at
  any intermediate level continues the chain; the 50 % majority bar
  only matters as the higher of the two ways to qualify.
- **Sub-threshold links break the chain.** A holds 15 % of H, H
  holds 30 % of root → A is **not** attributed root ownership; H
  isn't controlled by A.
- **Direct positions aggregate even below 25 %.** A person holding
  15 % + 15 % directly in the root is a UBO at 30 %.
- **Multiple controlled branches sum.** A controls X and Y; X holds
  30 %, Y holds 40 % of root → A's `effective_share_percent = 70`
  (each branch is independently a control link, and the root-edge
  shares add up).

Designed for KYC workflows where the freshest possible chain matters.

post.description:
Create a webhook, email, or async (poll-only) subscription for a single
company.

## Async (poll-only) subscriptions

Pass `"notification_type": null` (and omit both `webhook_url` and
`recipient_email`) to create a poll-only subscription. firmendata
performs the same change detection as for webhook/email, but instead of
calling out to your infrastructure on each change it records the
rendered payload as a `subscription_event`. Retrieve change events
afterwards via `GET /v1/subscriptions/{subscription_id}/events`,
where `subscription_id` is the value returned in this response (the
"job id" the response carries). `webhook_secret` is `null` for async
subscriptions — there is no outbound HTTP to sign.

## Webhook signature verification

firmendata signs **every** outgoing webhook request with HMAC-SHA256
so receivers can verify the request actually came from firmendata.
Verify on every incoming POST:

* `X-Firmendata-Signature: sha256=<hex>` — HMAC-SHA256 of
  `f"{X-Firmendata-Timestamp}.{raw_body}"` keyed by the
  `webhook_secret` returned in this response. Use a constant-time
  comparison.
* `X-Firmendata-Timestamp: <unix-seconds>` — reject values older than
  5 minutes to defeat replay attacks.
* `X-Firmendata-Delivery-Id: <uuid>` — idempotency key; safe to dedupe
  on. firmendata may re-POST the same delivery id after a transient
  receiver error.
* `X-Firmendata-Event-Type: <subscription_type>.updated` — e.g.
  `details.updated`, `doc_articles_of_association.updated`.

The response carries a one-time **`webhook_secret`**. Store it now —
it is **not** recoverable later. To rotate, delete the subscription
and re-create it.

## Defaults

* `mode` → `recurring` — see `mode` for the `one_time` alternative.
* `notification_type` → `null` (async, poll-only) — see `notification_type` for the `webhook` / `email` alternatives.
* `cadence` → `daily`.
* `language` → `en` (affects email rendering only).

## Email-mode rendering

When `notification_type=email`, the recipient's inbox shows:

* **Body table** with the company name, company id (`eu_id`),
  notification type, publish date, and — for `doc_*` subscriptions —
  the document type and file id. No authenticated `/v1/...` API URLs
  are rendered (email recipients carry no bearer token); a single
  public **"View company on FirmenData"** button links to
  `https://firmendata.com/{language}/company/{eu_id}`.
* **PDF attachment** (only for `doc_*` subscriptions) — the actual
  register document (Articles of Association / Anmeldung /
  Musterprotokoll / Liste der Gesellschafter) attached as a
  `application/pdf` MIME part. Recipients can save / forward / parse
  the file straight from their inbox.

Parsed-data subscriptions (`details`, `history`, `shareholders`,
`ubo`) deliver the body table only — the structured JSON itself
remains accessible via the v1 API for authenticated clients, and
the email recipient gets a human summary.

## Cadence semantics

`cadence` controls how often you wish to receive notifications. A
notification is only delivered when there is an actual change since
the previous successful delivery — no update means no notification.
`immediately` delivers an update as soon as it is detected, with a
service-level objective of within 1 hour of publication.
`daily` / `weekly` / `monthly` batch the check at the named cadence.

For `recurring` subscriptions, the **first** delivery is a snapshot
of the current state; after that, deliveries only fire on actual
updates.

For `one_time` subscriptions, `cadence` is the retry spacing while
we wait for the data to become available; the subscription stops on
the first successful delivery.

post.description:
Send one **real** sample notification — webhook **or** email — using
the same rendering, signing, and delivery path as production. **No
subscription is created**, no DB row is written, and no scrape runs.
Safe and cheap to call repeatedly from your CI / integration tests.

Pick the transport via `notification_type`:

* **`webhook`** — POSTs a signed JSON body to `webhook_url`. The
  request is always signed with the documented public test secret
  `firmendata_test_secret_do_not_use_in_production`. The HMAC recipe
  is identical to production, so any verification code that matches
  with this constant will also match a real per-subscription secret.
  Hard-code it in your unit tests; never reuse it for real
  subscriptions.
* **`email`** — composes the bilingual change-notification email
  (subject + HTML body) and SMTPs it to `recipient_email`. Subject
  is prefixed with `[TEST]`; the body carries an explicit "this is a
  test" banner so a human reading the inbox can't mistake it for a
  live update. For `doc_*` subscription types the response also
  attaches a tiny on-the-fly **sample PDF** so the customer's
  attachment-handling pipeline (parse Content-Type, save to disk,
  forward to S3, …) can be exercised end to end. In production the
  attachment is the real register PDF.

No retries — this is a fail-fast probe. The receiver's status, error
detail, and the exact bytes / headers / subject / body firmendata
sent are all returned, so you can diff them against your verification
routine offline if your endpoint isn't yet live.

`subscription_type` controls the payload shape, summary copy, and —
for `doc_*` types — the embedded download URL / file metadata block,
identical to what a real notification carries. `eu_id` is embedded in
the payload but does **not** need to be known to firmendata.

## Webhook payload faithfulness

Top-level `publish_date` and `links` are present on every delivery.
The per-type `data` block matches a production change delivery for
the same `subscription_type`:

* Parsed-data types (`details`, `history`, `shareholders`, `ubo`)
  deliver the **same response shape as the corresponding
  `GET /v1/companies/{eu_id}[/...]` endpoint**. When the
  `eu_id` you pass is known to firmendata the test endpoint embeds the
  real current data; when it does not, `data` is a sparse placeholder
  containing only `{eu_id}` — the field set is what varies, the schema
  does not.
* `doc_*` types deliver `{url, expires_at, file_id, file_type,
  fetched_at}` directly under `data`. In test mode the `url` points at
  the v1 documents endpoint (clearly identifiable as a test artifact);
  in production it is a 7-day presigned URL to the real document.

The only top-level difference between test and production is an extra
`_meta: {"test": true}` key — receivers that ignore unknown top-level
keys (recommended) need no test branch at all. The `subscription_id`
is a freshly-minted UUID, not a real id; treat it as opaque.

## Integration-test scenarios

Webhook only — pick via `delivery_scenario`:

* `success` (default) — single signed POST. Receiver should return 2xx.
* `retry_delivery` — two POSTs back-to-back with byte-identical body,
  signature, timestamp, and `X-Firmendata-Delivery-Id`. Mirrors how
  production retries look after a 5xx so you can verify your
  idempotent dedupe.
* `bad_signature` — single POST signed with a wrong secret. Your
  endpoint SHOULD reject with 4xx; that is the test passing.
* `stale_timestamp` — single POST whose `X-Firmendata-Timestamp` is
  10 minutes in the past. Your endpoint SHOULD reject with 4xx; that
  is the test passing.

Per-attempt detail (status, signature, timestamp, response excerpt)
is returned in `attempts[]` regardless of scenario.

## Sample receiver

A minimal listener that verifies the signature and prints the body —
drop into your test harness, point your `webhook_url` at it, and call
this endpoint to drive it.

### Python (Flask)

```python
# pip install flask
import hashlib
import hmac
import json
from flask import Flask, abort, request

WEBHOOK_SECRET = "firmendata_test_secret_do_not_use_in_production"
MAX_TIMESTAMP_SKEW_SECONDS = 5 * 60

app = Flask(__name__)


@app.post("/firmendata/webhook")
def receive_webhook():
    raw = request.get_data()
    sig = request.headers.get("X-Firmendata-Signature", "")
    ts = request.headers.get("X-Firmendata-Timestamp", "")

    expected = "sha256=" + hmac.new(
        WEBHOOK_SECRET.encode(),
        f"{ts}.".encode() + raw,
        hashlib.sha256,
    ).hexdigest()
    if not hmac.compare_digest(sig, expected):
        abort(401)

    # Replay protection — reject anything older than 5 minutes.
    import time
    if abs(int(time.time()) - int(ts or 0)) > MAX_TIMESTAMP_SKEW_SECONDS:
        abort(401)

    payload = json.loads(raw)
    print(
        f"[{payload['event_type']}] eu_id={payload['eu_id']} "
        f"delivery_id={request.headers['X-Firmendata-Delivery-Id']}"
    )
    print(json.dumps(payload, indent=2))
    return ("", 200)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    app.run(port=8080)
```

### Node.js (Express)

```js
// npm install express
import crypto from "node:crypto";
import express from "express";

const WEBHOOK_SECRET = "firmendata_test_secret_do_not_use_in_production";
const MAX_TIMESTAMP_SKEW_SECONDS = 5 * 60;

const app = express();

app.post(
  "/firmendata/webhook",
  express.raw({ type: "application/json" }),
  (req, res) => {
    const sig = req.header("X-Firmendata-Signature") ?? "";
    const ts = req.header("X-Firmendata-Timestamp") ?? "";

    const expected =
      "sha256=" +
      crypto
        .createHmac("sha256", WEBHOOK_SECRET)
        .update(`${ts}.${req.body.toString()}`)
        .digest("hex");
    const sigBuf = Buffer.from(sig);
    const expBuf = Buffer.from(expected);
    if (
      sigBuf.length !== expBuf.length ||
      !crypto.timingSafeEqual(sigBuf, expBuf)
    ) {
      return res.status(401).end();
    }

    if (Math.abs(Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000) - Number(ts || 0)) >
        MAX_TIMESTAMP_SKEW_SECONDS) {
      return res.status(401).end();
    }

    const payload = JSON.parse(req.body.toString());
    console.log(
      `[${payload.event_type}] eu_id=${payload.eu_id} ` +
        `delivery_id=${req.header("X-Firmendata-Delivery-Id")}`
    );
    console.log(JSON.stringify(payload, null, 2));
    res.status(200).end();
  }
);

app.listen(8080);
```

tags.description:
Find companies by free-text query and firmographic filters. Use `autocomplete` for fast suggestions and `search` for programmatic, filterable lookups.

### Filter values

Enum values are **case-insensitive** and tolerate the umlaut spellings German text arrives in, so `gmbh`, `muenchen` and `Baden-Wurttemberg` all resolve. Common abbreviations and alternative names work too (`NRW`, `Bavaria`, `Charlottenburg`, `Amtsgericht München`). A value that could mean two different things is rejected rather than guessed at — `Frankfurt` names two courts, so spell out `Frankfurt am Main` or `Frankfurt/Oder`.

### Repeating a filter

Filters that accept several values (`city`, `bundesland`, `rechtsform`, `wz_2025_code`, `industry_slug`, `legal_status`, `membership`, `tender_role`) OR-merge their values and accept any of the three encodings HTTP clients produce:

```
?rechtsform=GmbH&rechtsform=AG     repeated key
?rechtsform=GmbH,AG                comma-separated
?rechtsform[]=GmbH&rechtsform[]=AG bracket / indexed
```

Different filters are AND-merged. `city` and `bundesland` are the one exception: they form a single location filter, so a company matches when it is in any selected city **or** any selected federal state.

### Reading the financials

Each figure is resolved to the most recent filing that actually carries it, so they can come from *different* fiscal years — `revenue_year`, `profit_year`, `total_assets_year` and `employee_count_year` say which. Don't assume two of them share a year when computing a ratio. `financial_year` is a separate thing: the latest year the company filed anything at all.

Coverage differs sharply between the metrics, and it is not a data-quality gap — it follows German filing law. Small and medium-sized companies file abridged accounts under §§ 266, 276 HGB: a balance sheet, but no profit-and-loss statement, and no headcount. So the balance-sheet total is available for far more companies than revenue or employees are. **If you are filtering on company size, use `total_assets_min` / `total_assets_max` — the revenue bounds reach only the minority that publish a full P&L.**

tags.description:
Webhook and email subscriptions for company-data updates. firmendata checks the underlying source on the cadence you choose (`immediately` / `daily` / `weekly` / `monthly`) and only delivers a notification when there is an actual update — no update means no call.

Two kinds of `subscription_type`:

- **Parsed-data** types (`details`, `history`, `shareholders`, `ubo`) — the webhook body carries the publish-date and links to the v1 endpoints that serve parsed JSON.
- **Document** types (every `doc_*` value) — the webhook body carries a 7-day presigned download URL for the PDF, so the customer can grab the file directly with no follow-up API call.

Coverage is **not uniform** across legal forms: small GmbHs founded under the simplified procedure (§2 Abs. 1a GmbHG) replace the Articles of Association (Gesellschaftsvertrag / Satzung / Statut — the name varies by legal form) and the Liste der Gesellschafter with a single **Musterprotokoll** (model protocol). `shareholders` handles this transparently (auto-falls-back to the Musterprotokoll); the `doc_*` subscriptions do not — pick `doc_model_protocol` when you need the founding deed of a simplified-procedure company. The `SubscriptionType` schema documents the full per-value coverage table.

Every delivery (webhook or email) is recorded in the events history (`GET /v1/subscriptions/{id}/events`) — for webhooks the exact JSON body POSTed is persisted and can be replayed via `POST /v1/subscriptions/events/{event_id}/resend`.
